analysis.title: Investor Positioning and Flows: A Modest Bounce
key_insights: Aggregate equity positioning bounced modestly to the 26th percentile (-0.35sd) but remains underweight. The S&P 500 also bounced, attempting to return to the tight range held since August, but is still slightly below it.
Systematic strategies (-0.06sd, 37th percentile) cut exposure to a 7-month low on weaker trend signals and higher vol. Cuts were especially large in the Nasdaq 100, small caps and EM equities.

Discretionary positioning (-0.60sd, 13th percentile) rebounded off the bottom of its band but remains deeply underweight. The weakness goes beyond the resurgence in rates vol and is disconnected from fundamental drivers such as macro data surprises.
US macro data surprises (CESI) are at the 95th percentile since 2003, the strongest since 2023, when data defied recession forecasts. Data is now beating already robust expectations.

AAII sentiment (bull minus bear spread) is at the 8th percentile since 1987. Bullish responses (26th percentile) fell to an eight-week low and bearish responses (96th percentile) rose to an eight-week high.

In prior episodes of similarly weak AAII sentiment, S&P 500 returns the following week were mixed (median -0.4%, positive 47% of the time) and the following month typically positive (median +2.8%, positive 68% of the time). The text summary cites 66% and +3%, while the chart labels show 68% and 2.8%.

Tech (MCG & large-cap Tech) positioning bounced to -0.09sd (26th percentile) from its biggest underweight in 3.5 years. Tech remains in overshot territory slightly below its long-run trend channel. DB remains overweight Tech after upgrading it on Oct 30 2026.
Equity fund inflows of $98.3bn were a five-month high: US $63.6bn, EM $14.7bn, broad global $14.5bn, Japan $4.2bn, Europe $0.4bn. Tech sector funds took $8.9bn, a seventh straight week of inflows.

Bond fund inflows dropped sharply to an 18-month low (lowest since Liberation Day, Apr 2025). Broad-mandate bond funds saw outflows for the first time in nearly eight months. Money market funds saw outflows of $17.9bn after massive inflows the prior week.

CTAs cut their overall equity allocation to the lowest in seven months (42nd percentile). Nasdaq 100 positioning (14th percentile) flipped to net short for the first time in seven months. US small cap shorts increased (22nd percentile) and long positions in US large caps were pared (48th percentile).

Vol-control funds increased their equity allocation after last week's sharp cut (35th percentile) but remain well below recent highs. Their sensitivity to further selloffs eased. Risk parity equity allocation declined (70th percentile) while commodity allocation stayed extremely high (99th percentile).

Sector positioning: Energy jumped back to overweight (83rd percentile). Healthcare is at its biggest overweight in nine months (64th percentile). Utilities tumbled to an extreme underweight (1st percentile) and Consumer Staples is near the bottom of its range (9th percentile).

Small cap positioning slipped further underweight (-0.64sd, 19th percentile). The call-to-put volume ratio declined (48th percentile). S&P 500 3m skew declined after hitting a seven-month high last week.

CTAs' long US dollar positioning rose (95th percentile). Bond shorts were pared in the US (24th percentile), Europe (19th percentile) and Japan (41st percentile). Gold shorts were covered slightly (26th percentile) and copper longs (89th percentile) and oil longs (76th percentile) were trimmed.
DB S&P 500 forecasts: 2026 target 8000, 2026 EPS $362, 2027 EPS $430.

sector_views.rationale: DB upgraded Tech back to Overweight on Oct 30 2026. Positioning is low (26th percentile) and Tech is in overshot territory slightly below its long-run trend channel, with sector funds in a seventh straight week of inflows.
Positioning jumped back to overweight (83rd percentile), while energy sector funds saw outflows of $1.1bn. This is a positioning observation, not a DB rating.
Positioning rose to its biggest overweight in nine months (64th percentile) and funds had a seventh consecutive week of inflows ($0.9bn). This is a positioning observation, not a DB rating.
Positioning tumbled to an extreme underweight (-1.73sd, 1st percentile) and funds saw outflows of $0.8bn. This is a positioning observation, not a DB rating.

macro_indicators.reading: 95th percentile since 2003, at the top of its long-run range
macro_indicators.interpretation: Data is beating already robust expectations, the strongest surprise level since 2023. Discretionary positioning is far below what the 2010-2019 correlation of 34% with CESI would imply.
Sentiment is at the bottom of a four-decade range. Historically this has preceded positive S&P 500 returns over the following month.

macro_indicators.reading: Growth in the 30s, per DB's Q3 earnings publication titles
macro_indicators.interpretation: Fundamentals are strong while discretionary positioning is weak.

crypto_views: Weekly flows into cryptocurrency funds are charted (Figures 92 and 93), but the text gives no figures or commentary on crypto flows.
risk_factors: Rates vol resurgence has weighed on discretionary positioning (-62% correlation with MOVE).
Systematic de-risking could continue if trend signals weaken or vol rises further. Vol-control funds are well below recent highs, and sensitivity to selloffs has eased only somewhat.
The S&P 500 is still slightly below the tight range held since August.
Sentiment and discretionary positioning are at extremes. DB's history shows one-week returns after weak sentiment are mixed (median -0.4%, positive 47% of the time).
charts_described: Figure 2 plots US CESI against large-cap discretionary positioning, with a 2010-2019 correlation of 34%. Discretionary positioning is significantly below levels implied by macro data surprises.
Figure 3 shows the US CESI at the 95th percentile since 2003, with the last comparable strength in 2023.
Figure 4 plots the inverted MOVE index against large-cap discretionary positioning, with a -62% correlation since 2021.
Figure 6 shows S&P 500 median returns after the AAII spread fell to extreme lows (episodes since 2010): 1 week median -0.4% (positive 47%), 1 month median 2.8% (positive 68%).
Figure 7 shows the MCG & Tech ratio to the rest of the S&P 500 against a trend growth of 14.2% annualized with a +/-10% band, with Tech in overshot territory.
vol_and_positioning: Aggregate equity positioning is -0.35sd (26th percentile), discretionary is -0.60sd (13th percentile) and systematic is -0.06sd (37th percentile), the lowest in 7 months.
Rates vol (MOVE index) has a -62% correlation since 2021 with large-cap discretionary equity positioning. The resurgence in rates vol has weighed on discretionary positioning.
Systematic positioning has a -77% correlation with S&P 500 1m realized vol, and higher vol drove the systematic cuts.

CTAs' Nasdaq 100 positioning (14th percentile) flipped to net short for the first time in seven months. The S&P 500 is at the 48th percentile, Russell 2000 at the 22nd, Europe at the 60th, Japan at the 26th and EM at the 34th.
Vol-control funds' equity allocation is at the 35th percentile and their sensitivity to a 2% selloff has eased.
S&P 500 3m 90-110 skew fell after a seven-month high last week. The call/put volume ratio (5d ma) is at the 48th percentile and total net call volume is at the 84th percentile since 2010.
Net call volume fell sharply in index options and modestly in single-stock options, and rose modestly in ETF options. Within single stocks it rose in MCG & Tech and declined in Consumer Cyclicals.
The basket of stocks with the highest prior-week net call volume modestly outperformed the market. The most-shorted basket was choppy and in line with the market.

Large-cap mutual fund beta to the S&P 500 is at the 25th percentile (1m) and 22nd percentile (3m). Equity long/short hedge fund beta is at the 56th percentile (1m) and 64th percentile (3m), against a 3m average of 0.29.
Short interest data (as of Oct 30) is charted for the Russell 3000, S&P 500, Nasdaq 100 and Russell 2000, but the text gives no levels.
Announced S&P 500 buybacks: $192bn weekly/3m-sum figure on the chart and $228bn over the last 3 months by sector.

tension_points.bull_case: Discretionary positioning (13th percentile) and sentiment (8th percentile) are at extreme lows while macro data surprises are at the 95th percentile. Prior weak-sentiment episodes were followed by positive S&P 500 returns over the next month (median +2.8%, positive 68% of the time). Equity fund inflows hit $98.3bn.
